variant.name: ALOHA Stationary (Trossen Robotics / Interbotix ROS 2 'aloha' package)
variant.rationale: Best-documented public ALOHA configuration with machine-readable kinematics and inertials: official URDF/xacro + meshes for the ALOHA-specific arm variants (aloha_vx300s, aloha_wx250s), official bringup with workcell transforms, and official per-arm spec pages. The Kyoto University configuration could not be confirmed from public evidence. Original Stanford ALOHA (tonyzhaozh/aloha) and ALOHA 2 MJCF (mujoco_menagerie) are different variants and are NOT mixed in.

complete_robot_definition: The complete documented mechanical assembly = 4 arms (2 follower ALOHA ViperX-300 6DOF, 2 leader ALOHA WidowX-250 6DOF) with every URDF link and joint (including grippers, finger mimic, leader handle), mounted in the world frame with the bringup transforms. Excluded because no public machine-readable geometry exists for this variant: table/frame, cameras, gravity compensators.
mount_source: Interbotix/aloha launch/aloha_bringup.launch.py static_transform_publisher world->*/base_link (identity rotation). Classified 'verified' as published; it is the ROS visualisation frame layout, not a surveyed physical workcell measurement.
missing_information: Gripper motor-to-finger linkage: URDF models the gripper prop rotation (continuous) and finger translation (prismatic) as independent joints; the mechanical coupling is not in the URDF. aloha/constants.py gives a calibrated linear map only between the ALOHA close/open points.

Gearbox ratios, motor constants, friction and efficiency of the Dynamixel servos (datasheet values not ingested yet; URDF <dynamics friction=0.1 damping=0.1> are generic defaults, not identified values).
Workcell frame, table and camera mounts for this variant.
Placeholder inertials (mass 0.001 kg, I = 1e-4 kg m^2) on ee_arm_link, fingers_link, ee_gripper_link: rendered as massless frames.
assumptions: Gripper prop (continuous) joint held at 0 rad in baseline experiments (no documented coupling).
Followers and leaders use the same START_ARM_POSE (as in aloha/constants.py).

discrepancies.resolution: trajectories clamp to the URDF limit

discrepancies.item: spec page servo-ID table vs servo configuration table
discrepancies.detail: Joint-limit table lists Wrist Angle as ID 6 / Forearm Roll ID 7; servo table lists 6 forearm_roll / 7 wrist_angle. URDF joint order (forearm_roll before wrist_angle) matches the servo table.
